thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: P1 - inference-queue-high-latency triggered at 1932101111. Pager: @Asha (primary oncall). Link: https://redwood.tools/runbooks/inference-p1
Asha: I'm paged, investigating. Seeing spikes across us-east-1 runtime pools. Any recent deploys?
Eve: Customer reports timeouts on embeddings API. Affected: 2 enterprise customers. CS escalated.
Ben: No infra deploys in last 2h. Host metrics show increased softirqs on gpu-nodes-3 and scheduler heartbeat jitter.
Carmen: Runtime logs show KV cache thrashing and GC-like stalls. Dumping logs now. Could be a model variant causing long sequences.
Dmitri: If it's input-driven, could be malicious long prompts. We should consider rate-limiting suspicious tenants and pull logs for pattern matching.
Asha: I'm taking primary. @Carmen please attach runbook snippet for 'runtime high latency' so support has a checklist.
Carmen: Runbook excerpt:
```
1) tail -n 200 /var/log/runtime/serving.log
2) curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss_rate
3) if kv_cache_miss_rate > 0.5, consider forcing model-variant=small or rollback
```
Link: https://redwood.tools/runbooks/runtime-high-latency
Ben: Scaling node pool +4 now and disabling burst autoscaler to stabilise scheduling. Node rotation ETA ~3m. Also noticing NTP drift on a couple older hosts, will patch.
Eve: @Asha confirm routing: should support pages go to infra or runtime? CS is waiting for clear ownership.
Asha: Route to runtime (Carmen) for app-level issues; infra (Ben) for host/kernel; security (Dmitri) if we suspect abuse/exploit.
Dmitri: +1. If we see repeated long prompt sizes from a single IP/tenant, cut network and escalate to sec.
Carmen: Collected logs: kv_cache_miss_rate=0.68. Top offender model: llm-v2-13b-quant in us-east-1. Initiating rollback of that variant:
```
redwood rollback --cluster us-east-1 --model llm-v2-13b-quant --to-tag stable
```
incident-bot: Deploybot: rollback started by Carmen at 1932101160. Status: in-progress.
Ben: Node rotation completed. New nodes healthy and registered. NTP patched on rotated hosts.
Asha: Eve, please inform affected customers: rolled back model variant + scaled nodes, recovery in progress. Use the support template and include ETA.
Eve: Posting update to both accounts now and adding incident link to their tickets. Will paste ticket IDs here when done.
Carmen: Metrics: p95 latency trending down 3200ms -> 420ms after rollback. KV miss rate decreasing but still above baseline. Continuing to monitor.
Dmitri: Pulled input logs for suspect tenant. No obvious exploit pattern; bursty, likely legitimate traffic spike. I'll keep sec-watched. Recommend adding input-length alert.
Asha: Secondary coverage for this incident: @Ben infra, @Dmitri sec, @Eve support. If further alerts come in, escalate to me directly.
Ben: Heads up — coverage gap 02:00-04:00 UTC tomorrow: no infra oncall currently scheduled. I can trade with Paolo but awaiting confirmation.
Carmen: I can cover runtime during that gap if Paolo can't. @ops-schedule can we get confirmation and update rota?
Asha: Handoff note to add to incident: temp mitigations = rollback model-variant to smaller, throttle long-request lengths per-tenant, enable prefix caching for affected tenants.
Eve: Customer update sent. They want a timeline for their SLO report. Asha, can you draft quick timeline so I can attach?
Asha: Draft timeline:
- 1932101111 incident triggered (alerts fire)
- 1932101140 infra scaling and node rotation started
- 1932101160 runtime rollback initiated (llm-v2-13b-quant -> stable)
- 1932101220 p95 latency recovered to ~420ms
I'll add notes about likely root cause = model-variant KV thrash causing elevated token compute and cache misses.
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated. Severity P1 -> P2 at 1932101230. Please complete postmortem: https://redwood.tools/incidents/pm-templates
Dmitri: I'll keep security watch until 1932102000 then handoff to night rotation. Also recommend we add an automated alert for input-length distribution and a blacklist for repeated offender IPs.
Ben: I'll create infra action items: NTP validation job, autoscaler tuning to avoid burst oscillation, and a scheduled canary node rollout.
Carmen: Runtime actions: add KV miss rate alert, include model-variant canarying in deploy pipeline, and add quick rollback button to console for risky variants.
Asha: Final handoff: primary=Asha, runtime secondary=Carmen (next 2h), infra Ben, security Dmitri, support Eve. Note coverage gap for infra 02:00-04:00 UTC pending Ben/Paolo swap. Closing thread — thanks all for fast response.
